title: Public structured-export API over the corpus
context: open-coding-curriculum is an open CC-BY (prose) / MIT (code) curriculum of beginner programming lessons with graded, runnable exercises across languages. Every exercise carries a reference solution proven correct in CI (solutionVerified:true), learner code runs zero-install in-browser via WASM, and all content is machine-readable structured data so third parties can build on it. The project targets absolute beginners — self-learners, public-library patrons, under-resourced school students, career-changers — and operates under a donated-compute lane with no server-side execution of learner code and no partner confirmed yet (verifiedNeed:false). If downstream demand for programmatic access to the corpus emerges (course builders, LMS integrations, research tools), a structured-export API makes the CC-BY corpus far more useful than a static file download. This is deferred until downstream demand is confirmed to avoid over-engineering.
objective: Design and implement a public, read-only structured-export API over the validated curriculum corpus, enabling downstream tools to query lessons, exercises, and metadata programmatically — only if confirmed downstream demand exists.
acceptanceCriteria: At least one confirmed downstream consumer (course builder, LMS, or research tool) is documented before implementation begins.
API is read-only and serves only the validated, published corpus (no draft or unverified content).
API responses include all license and provenance metadata (outputLicense, isOriginal, sources) so downstream reusers can comply with CC-BY requirements.
API is versioned; breaking changes require a new version path.
API documentation is public and includes usage examples and attribution requirements.
No learner data or PII is exposed by or stored by the API.
pnpm build && pnpm test && pnpm lint pass.
output: A deployed, documented, versioned read-only API over the validated curriculum corpus, with CC-BY provenance metadata and no learner PII.
